subject: Logic
title: Rational Choice Theory
description: Learn Rational Choice Theory in one minute.

hook.text: Economists assumed humans always maximize self-interest. Then researchers watched real people—and found chaos.

buildup.text: Rational choice theory says people pick the option that gives them the highest expected benefit.

discovery.text: It's an idealization—a benchmark for how a perfectly logical agent would behave.

twist.text: Real humans use shortcuts, follow emotions, and often prefer a sure small gain over a risky larger one.

climax.text: The theory isn't wrong—it's incomplete. It describes what we should do, not always what we actually do.

punchline.text: The rational ideal is a compass, not a portrait.

quiz.question: What does rational choice theory assume?
options: People select options that maximize expected benefit
